notes:
Summary: Large developer platform company building an in-IDE copilot used by 2,000+ engineers. Primary concerns: consistent sub-50ms char-streaming latency in the IDE, predictable per-seat economics, and strong key management + audit trail.

Product fit & priorities:
- Must support streaming token-by-token for line completions and inline suggestions (low jitter).
- Need model/version pinning per team + gradual rollouts (canary) — stable dev experience required.
- Strong interest in per-seat unit economics: want a hybrid license (min seats) + overage per-token. Finance cautious on high tail usage (batch runs, CI).
- Cost optimization ask: quantization profiles for medium-length completions (128-1024 tokens), automatic KV/prefix caching across sessions, and recommendation engine for batching vs latency tradeoffs.

Security/compliance:
- Requires SSO/SAML integration with SCIM provisioning.
- KMS customer-managed keys preferred, need proof of key separation for log ingestion.
- Data residency conversation: staging infra in na, production in us-west and eu-west.

Quotes / paraphrase:
- "We can't tolerate frequent model drift; devs expect identical completions across versions."
- "If we can save ~30% on per-seat costs via quantization and smarter caching, procurement will sign faster."

technical_notes: POC scope: 2 Dedicated nodes (A100 equivalent), 50 seat token load, simulate IDE streaming with 100ms think-time
Metrics to measure: p50/p95 per-token latency, jitter, token cost per suggestion, KV cache hit rate
Experiment plan: run quantization profiles (int8, q4f) and measure predicted quality delta using internal eval set
Routing policy ask: prefer lower-cost variant for non-latency-critical completions; fallback to high-accuracy model for canary teams
business_case: Objective: replace homegrown completions stack and unify inference to reduce ops burden. Expected ROI from reduced infra spend + faster on-boarding. Finance requires scenario: per-seat capped + 20% overage for peak months.
po_note: Procurement expects final SOW + security addendum. Targeting pilot contract (3 month) then expand to enterprise license.
